goal: Build a complete, polished Brick Breaker (Arkanoid-style) browser game with exactly 20 distinct playable levels of increasing difficulty. Include keyboard and pointer/touch controls, score and lives, pause/resume, restart, level progression, and a victory state after level 20. Deliver a runnable project with README instructions and meaningful automated tests verifying all 20 levels and core gameplay. For automated acceptance testing, expose a read-only window.__gameState updated every frame: { phase: 'menu'|'playing'|'paused'|'levelComplete'|'gameOver'|'victory', level, totalLevels, score, lives, paddle: { x }, ball: { x, y }, bricksRemaining }, and window.__gameTest = { completeLevel(), loseBall() } hooks that clear the current level / miss the ball through the game's own logic. Start with Enter or Space, move with ArrowLeft/ArrowRight, pause with P, restart with Enter or R.

requirements.behavior: Exactly 20 distinct playable levels; inspect level definitions and evidence of different layouts/increasing difficulty, not file count alone.
Start via real keyboard; keyboard and pointer/touch move paddle; ball travels and collides with paddle/walls/bricks. Actual brick removal increases score, not a hook or score change alone.
Pause freezes gameplay; resume continues; naturally missing ball removes a life; zero lives shows game over.
Clearing levels progresses in order to 20 then victory; deterministic hook checks supplement at least one natural transition/collision check.
Restart from victory and game-over resets level, score, lives and transient state; new run remains playable.
Contract read-only state matches rendered gameplay; hooks route through ordinary game logic, never independent artificial score/phase updates.
Responsive readable UI, instructions, keyboard/pointer/touch controls; screenshots plus actual input evidence on desktop/mobile.
Build and real automated tests pass; no fatal browser errors or missing resources; clean-copy install/run documented. Broken collision/input/victory/restart fixtures must fail relevant acceptance.
